item.title: Duval Dispatch: Jags earn ‘A’ in blowout win over Colts
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Runningback Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs in for a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jaguars took advantage of a Colts teams on that Sunday that just finished sending two of their cornerstone players elsewhere. Jacksonville won 42-7 and may have just forced the Colts to continue selling off their best remaining pieces on the roster to fully embrace the upcoming rebuild. For their efforts, CBS Sports’ John Breech gave them a shining “A” grade in his weekly report card series. ‘‘It took eight weeks, but Bayshul Tuten finally had his breakout game, and it was impressive: The Jaguars running back topped 100 yards on the ground with a TD, and he added another 55 receiving yards with another TD. This was exactly what the Jags were hoping to see from Tuten when they let Travis Etienne leave in free agency. Tuten has been good this year and it looks like he might be ready to make the jump to great. Defensively, the Jags came out of their bye on fire: They harassed Daniel Jones to the tune of three sacks and Rayuan Lane III added a 92-yard pick-six that essentially iced the game in the second quarter (Yes, this game was over in the second quarter). The blowout win meant the Jags could bench several starters in the fourth quarter, a huge perk for a Jacksonville team that has to turn around and play on Thursday night.” Do you think this was the correct grade? Should they have received a “+” to go with their A? Let us know below! item.title: England call up Spencer and Randall as injuries hit
item.description: Ben Spencer and Harry Randall have 19 and 14 England caps respectively [Getty Images] Ben Spencer and Harry Randall have been named in England's squad for this month's Nations Championship after injury ruled Northampton nines Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland out of Sunday's match with Australia. Mitchell pulled up with a hamstring issue in Saints' win over Gloucester on Saturday, while uncapped prospect McParland, 21, picked up a calf injury in last week's training camp. McParland, who would have toured with England in July but for a severe cut to his leg in the Prem final win over Exeter, could still be in contention for England's matches against Japan and New Zealand on 14 and 21 November respectively. Mitchell will have a scan on his hamstring on Monday to assess the extent of his injury and subsequent lay-off. The 29-year-old has suffered three previous hamstring injuries already this year. Leicester's Jack van Poortvliet, who started all three of England's summer Tests, seems set to continue as first-choice scrum-half. England are facing a possible change at fly-half, with first-choice Fin Smith struggling with a calf problem and Marcus Smith and George Ford competing to deputise in his possible absence. Elsewhere Saracens' Theo Dan has seen off competition from Nathan Jibulu, Jamie Blamire and Gabriel Oghre to secure the third hooker spot in the squad. Dan comes in in place of Bath's Kepu Tuipulotu who, like McParland, picked up an injury during last week's three-day training camp. Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson and Exeter wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso are also included after successfully negotiating injury comebacks for their clubs this weekend. Midfield is the area of most selection intrigue with Gloucester's Will Joseph, who won his solitary previous cap back in 2022, and Sale's Joe Marchant, who has returned to eligibility after three seasons playing in France, included. Bath centre pair Ollie Lawrence and Max Ojomoh, who both starred in last autumn's clean sweep, are omitted and there is no space for 20-year-old Saracens wing Noah Caluori. After the matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, England will play a fourth Test against an as-yet-undecided southern hemisphere opponent in the play-off finals weekend of the new Nations Championship format. Liverpool, 2018/19 Jurgen Klopp's best Liverpool sides are often remembered for their firepower, but the Reds proved hugely difficult to break down too. Trent Alexander-Arnold and Andy Robertson excelled at both ends of the pitch, while Alisson Becker and Virgil van Dijk were colossal during the 2018/19 campaign. Van Dijk was named PFA Player of the Year and Ballon d'Or runner-up , as Liverpool finished second with a record 97 points, losing only one game and conceding just 22 goals. item.title: Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi feature in Tilak Varma-led India A squad for Rising Stars Asia Cup
item.description: NEW DELHI: The BCCI on Monday announced a strong 15-member India A squad for the upcoming ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Doha, with explosive opener Abhishek Sharma and teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the prominent names in the lineup. Tilak Varma has been appointed captain, while experienced batter Rajat Patidar will serve as his deputy for the tournament, scheduled to be held in Qatar from November 19 to 29. The squad features several players who were part of India's recent T20I assignment against New Zealand, which the senior side won 3-2. The inclusion of the 15-year-old Sooryavanshi is particularly noteworthy, with the youngster continuing to attract attention for his aggressive batting and rapid rise through the domestic and age-group ranks. Abhishek, Sooryavanshi headline batting firepower India A have assembled a formidable batting group, with Abhishek and Sooryavanshi expected to provide explosive options at the top of the order. Captain Tilak and Patidar add experience and stability to the middle order, while Rinku Singh brings his reputation as a finisher. Prabhsimran Singh and Kumar Kushagra are the two wicketkeeping options in the squad. The all-rounders' department features Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey and Tanush Kotian, providing the team with multiple batting and bowling options. The pace attack will feature Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav and Arshad Khan. — BCCI (@BCCI) India A placed in Group B with Pakistan A India A have been placed in Group B alongside Pakistan A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). They will begin their campaign against Nepal on November 20 at the West End Park International Stadium in Doha before facing arch-rivals Pakistan A at the same venue on November 22. Their final group-stage fixture will be against the UAE on November 24. Group A comprises Bangladesh A, Sri Lanka A, Afghanistan A and Hong Kong, China. The top two teams from each group will progress to the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27, while the final will be played on November 29. With a blend of established performers, international experience and exciting young talent, India A will look to make a strong impression in the tournament and challenge for the title. India A squad for Rising Stars Asia Cup Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Prabhsimran Singh [WK], Tilak Varma [C], Rajat Patidar [VC], Rinku Singh, Kumar Kushagra [WK], Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav, Arshad Khan

item.title: Kansas Named Finalist For 2027 Five-Star Forward
item.description: Kansas Basketball remains in the mix for one of the top players left in the 2027 class. Five-star small forward Malachi Jordan remains focused on three schools and the Jayhawks are in the mix. Jordan will now decide between Kansas, St. John’s, and Vanderbilt. Jordan is currently ranked as the No. 8 player in Florida and No. 6 small forward in the nation, via 247Sports Composite. Adam Finkelstein of 247Sports highlighted Jordan’s physical gifts when writing his scouting report: “Jordan is one of the most physically gifted prospects in the class. He has good positional size, a powerful frame, long arms (6-foot-11-plus wingspan), and explosive vertical athleticism. He’s coming off an EYBL season in which he averaged just 10.8 points on 37/15/56 shooting with 2.6 assists against 3.3 turnovers, but actually has underrated skill and even feel. For Jordan, it’s all about playing in the flow. When he’s not trying to do too much, he has enough touch to make open rhythm shots, be a straight-line downhill driver, and even underrated passer. He’s also a violent finisher and lob threat whenever he can get to two feet. Conversely though, when he gets caught up in trying to prove himself, or isn’t utilized correctly, he gets inefficient. So, it’s not so much about his ability to see or make the right play, but more about a willingness to do it.“ Jordan last visited St. John’s at the end of October. This came after official visits to Kansas, Vanderbilt, USC, and Tennessee. After these visits, he has now named a final three and Kansas is in play for a big fish in the class.

item.title: Tenerife player in intensive care with head injury
item.description: Tenerife won promotion back to Spain's Segunda Division in May 2026 [Getty Images] Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel is in a stable condition in intensive care after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The 30-year-old suffered the injury in added time of Tenerife's home fixture against Andorra following a collision with visiting goalkeeper Jesus Owono. Spanish media, including Marca , reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital. A statement from Tenerife said the Madrid-born De Miguel was admitted to the University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria and was "stable despite the severity of his condition". Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 and seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred. Owono had run towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel. De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital. Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears. The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match. A statement from Andorra said: "We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match. "We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family and Tenerife." Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

item.title: Leeds to pay tribute to fan who died before match
item.description: Colin Westby had supported the club for more than 50 years [Leeds United] Leeds United have said they will pay tribute to a fan who died after suffering a medical emergency in the stands before the team's game against Manchester United. Colin Westby was watching the match at Elland Road on Sunday 18 October when he fell ill and was taken to hospital, the club said. Posting on social media, the club said the 68-year-old was placed in a medically induced coma but, after a "period of unresponsiveness", the decision was made to withdraw life support. The club said a tribute would be held to Colin in the 68th minute of their next Premier League fixture against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. A statement said: "Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years. "The thoughts of everyone at Leeds United are with Colin's family and friends at this sad time. "We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November." item.title: Pistons' Ron Holland finding ways to overcome a 'slow start' to season
item.description: CHARLOTTE — Cade Cunningham and Ron Holland II were among the last players to leave the practice floor at the Henry Ford Pistons Performance Center on Oct. 22. The two Dallas natives engaged in an easygoing one-on-one game, during which Holland made a contested fadeaway 3-pointer over Cunningham. Cunningham stayed calm when Holland started celebrating the shot because he knew the third-year forward had spent the entire summer working to become a better shooter. However, when the lights shone brightly through the first five games of the season, Holland looked nothing like the player who had spent countless hours in the gym. He started the season by missing his first six attempts from beyond the arc, a streak that ended at 3:55 in the third quarter when Holland made his first 3-pointer of the season off an assist from Kevin Huerter. The most modest fan at Barclays Center on Friday night reacted similarly to Cunningham, because of the confidence Holland showed on the shot. For Holland, however, the basket was a relief. "It was the first one of the season. As y'all can see, I am never going to stop shooting because I work on my shot every day," Holland said. "It was good to finally see one go in to get into a rhythm and see what it feels like. Now, it's all about moving on to the next game. I am not going to let one shot determine who I am as a player, but I am going to keep shooting." Bickerstaff to bench him earlier than usual while playing other players in his minutes. At the same time, these difficulties began to weigh on Holland's mind, as he realized he was not meeting the expectations set for him at the start of the season. "It's a long season, but I am here to work and to continue getting better. Grow with this team. Grow as a player. Grow as a man. But I have a long way to go and a lot to do, and I am excited about that." Holland played a key role in the Pistons' 60-win campaign last season. His development from his rookie year to his second season earned him a larger role on the team. He played in 78 regular-season games, averaging 19.9 minutes. He finished the season as one of four players in the top 30 in steals with 92 takeaways. Holland seemed ready to contribute significantly to Detroit's postseason efforts but spent most of the playoffs on the bench after Bickerstaff cut him from the rotation. Holland averaged 6.4 minutes over 14 playoff games. Most of his playing time came when the outcome was already decided. " Some time in this league, you can do all the right things, but that does not mean it's going to come together," Duncan Robinson said. "He had had some really positive stretches that we have seen. We all know the kind of player that he is and what he is capable of. When he plays with confidence, he is a different player." Even amid his struggles through the first five games, Holland proved his value by refusing to let it define his game. Holland attributes his continued productivity to the confidence he gets from both the coaching staff and his teammates. In the Pistons' 128-111 victory over the Miami Heat on Oct. 23, Holland contributed with five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 22 minutes, which was vital since Detroit lost its All-Star center, Jalen Duren, to a hamstring injury. Holland's performance against the Heat was a strong rebound after he played under three minutes against the Boston Celtics due to a slow start and early foul trouble in the team's season opener. Two nights later in the Pistons' victory over the Philadelphia 76ers, Holland was the primary defender on Jaylen Brown, limiting the All-NBA forward to 16 points on 5-for-20 shooting. More: Pistons' Duncan Robinson is off to a sizzling start to the season "His impact in winning plays and the effort that he plays with, the way that he attacks the rim, runs the floor, and defends — those are the things I've been impressed with and pleased with," Bickerstaff said. "Now, it's about him getting comfortable with what we are doing offensively, which is new. Figuring out where he fits and gets his touches, where his shots are going to come from, but it is the same for everybody right now." In his 18-point performance against the Nets, Holland had one of the best shooting displays of his career. He shot 6-for-10 from the field, including 2-for-5 from deep, and added four steals. He also led the Pistons during a dominant third quarter, scoring 12 points and helping Detroit outscore the Nets 36-17. Holland's performance against the Nets earned him BTA honors (Belt To Ass) as he left Barclays Center with the team's WWE championship belt draped over his shoulder. The handover was appropriate, as Cunningham — the previous holder — acknowledged Holland's performance during the team's post-game celebration, creating a full-circle moment for the Texas natives. "I know who I am and the energy I bring to this team," Holland said. "I am here with the franchise I want to be with, and I know they believe in me." coty.davis@detroitnews.com @cotydavis_24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Pistons' Ron Holland finding ways to overcome a 'slow start' to season

item.description: Charlie Smyth returned to the New Orleans Saints' practice roster for the new NFL season [Getty Images] Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Dan Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns. Carlson has been the Saints' first-choice kicker this season but the 31-year-old has struggled for consistency. Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in County Down, made his NFL debut last season but returned to the practice roster after the Saints elected to bring in Carlson for the start of the current campaign. But Carlson's form has opened the door for Smyth to potentially return to the playing roster, and Moore said both he and his coaching staff will "evaluate the field goal situation and opportunities". Moore said that the Saints had not brought any additional kickers into their squad, which leaves Smyth and Carlson in contention to start against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. "That's something we'll have to work through and discuss to find the best solution for Sunday," said Moore. "We'll see how it goes. We'll have some kicking sessions throughout this week and we'll see where we are at." Former Gaelic footballer Smyth made 12 of 16 field goals and was successful on each of his 13 extra-point attempts as a starter last season, after his historic NFL debut last November But he had a mixed pre-season and Carlson was selected to be the Saints' first choice after a kicking competition ahead of the NFL season. But Carlson has a success rate of 66% this season from 12 field goal attempts and his only perfect game with the boot came in September when he landed three kicks against the Baltimore Ravens. item.title: Luton and Barnsley fined over mass confrontation
item.description: Luton boss Jack Wilshere and Barnsley manager Daniel Stendel were among those to clash at the end of last month's fixture [Getty Images] Luton and Barnsley have been fined £13,500 by the Football Association (FA) after a "mass confrontation" during the October League One fixture between the sides. Jack Wilshere's Luton won 2-1 at Kenilworth Road, but a melee broke out at full-time after Barnsley's Amani Richards thought he had won a penalty only to be booked for simulation. In a statement, the FA said both sides "failed to ensure that their players and/or technical area staff did not behave in a way which was improper and/or provocative after the full-time whistle." Luton and Barnsley admitted the charges, and an independent commission ruled on imposing fines on both clubs. Luton Town 2-1 Barnsley All the latest Luton Town news

item.title: 'Never about the money': Nikita Kucherov addresses trade request from Lightning for first time
item.description: 'Never about the money': Nikita Kucherov addresses trade request from Lightning for first time originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NHL world was shaken on Friday when Elliotte Friedman reported that Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov requested a trade from the franchise. Kucherov is set to hit free agency at the end of the season, and his negotiations with the Lightning on a new contract have clearly gone sour. Although Kucherov has been in the NHL since 2011, he has produced at least 100 points in each of the last four seasons, leading the league twice and winning the league MVP award last year. Additionally, star NHL players have received significant raises in the offseason, with Cale Makar becoming the first player to make $20 million per season. Kucherov is very much in play to surpass Makar's deal and become the league's highest-paid player, especially if he hits the market on July 1. While Kucherov's salary is the main talking point, the forward said that money isn't why he is requesting a trade. Here's why Kucherov said he requested a trade from the Lightning. MORE : Grading the Devils trade for Connor Hellebuyck Nikita Kucherov on trade request On Monday, Nikita Kucherov addressed his trade request with the media for the first time, and the star forward made it clear why he made that decision. Kucherov said the issue is not about money, and instead a product of a deteriorating relationship between him and general manager Julien BriseBois. "It was never about the money for me, more about poor communication and respect," Kucherov said. "Over the last four months, we only have had two conversations. Julien, in the end, made it clear I'm free to walk on July 1st." Encina (@EddieInTheYard) November 2, 2026 BriseBois has notably been a tough negotiator in his time as the Lightning general manager, and he has not been afraid to move on from franchise greats. Since BriseBois took over as GM in 2010, the Lightning have either traded or let walk in free agency players like Marty St. Louis, Steven Stamkos, and Ryan McDonagh. The Kucherov negotiations appear no different, and it could mean that the star is ready for a fresh start. While he is already 33 years old, Kucherov is the reigning Hart Trophy winner and still one of the great scorers in the entire league. Unlike other players who requested a trade, Kucherov is still playing games with Tampa Bay, as it appears he has separated his negotiations with the GM from his performance with his teammates. It is still early in the NHL season, but a Kucherov trade would already shake the league. MORE: Panthers' Brady Tkachuk eggs on booing crowd, scores in return to Ottawa

item.description: Who was the Milwaukee area's top prep athlete last week? You tell us. You can vote for the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel high school athlete of the week until 3 p.m. Nov. 7. Do not send official votes to these addresses. Oconomowoc's Connor Haen was the winner of last week's poll. Here are the nominees. If the poll does not display, refresh your browser . Charlotte Bartelak, fr., New Berlin Eisenhower girls cross-country The freshman led a program-first WIAA state team title-winning effort in Division 2 by leading the Lions with her time of 18 minutes, 44 seconds to place seventh individually in her state debut. Morell Jackson, sr., Racine Case football The state's sixth-leading rusher had another masterful performance in Racine Case's 49-0 rout of Kenosha Indian Trail on Friday, Oct. 30. The area's leading rusher tallied just 13 carries, but ran for an area-leading 234 yards and four touchdowns for the Eagles. The victory for Jackson and the Eagles marked the first time in program history Case will play in the state quarterfinal round in its seventh all-time playoff appearance since 1980. Kaitlyn Marx, jr., Franklin girls volleyball For the third time in program history, Franklin will play at the WIAA girls volleyball state tournament after winning a five-set thriller in the sectional final against Burlington 25-8, 22-25, 21-25, 25-22, 15-13. Marx was fantastic for the Sabers in their comeback after falling behind two sets to one with 20 digs, 19 kills, seven aces and three assists. item.title: Who's still committed in Florida State's 2027 recruiting class?
item.description: The Mike Norverll era is over at Florida State , but what will happen with his final recruiting class ? Florida State currently has 14 players committed in the 2027 class, which is ranked 50th in the nation on the 247Sports composite rankings . The last time Florida State was ranked outside the top 20 was the 2021 class, when the Seminoles finished with the No. 23 class. That was an extremely strange recruiting cycle as it was limited because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The reasons why this class is ranked in the middle of the pack nationally is simple: Uncertainty. Three-star North Carolina wide receiver Majay Thompson decommitted from the Seminoles just a few hours before Norvell was fired. More: Florida State struggled to land elite in-state recruits under Norvell The lack of certainty around Norvell's job security has made recruiting very difficult. Now that he's been fired, more questions have to be answered. Who will be the next coach? When will the next coach be hired? UCF didn't have a coach during the early signing period in 2024. USF hired Brian Hartline during the first day of the early signing period in 2025. What scheme will the new coach run? Who will the assistant coaches be? What's the NIL budget? Will the new coach want the players currently committed? All of these things — and more — will impact what players decide to be Seminoles in December and February. item.title: Hawks Must Fix Their Slow Starts To Beat A Battered Pacers Team
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Both the Atlanta Hawks and Indiana Pacers are limping into Monday night with their worst losses of the season. The Hawks got crushed on the road 121-99 by the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday, while the Pacers fell 98-90 to a winless Brooklyn Nets team on Sunday. This matchup is a battle between two teams trying to snap skids, but the Hawks have a specific problem that must be fixed before tipoff. Johnson’s ankle and a thin frontcourt The biggest story is whether All-Star forward Jalen Johnson will play. He is listed as questionable with a left ankle sprain after exiting the game against New Orleans in the third quarter. If Johnson sits, the Hawks lose their best player and their frontcourt becomes dangerously thin. Per Sports Illustrated , Jock Landale is already ruled out with a left hip strain, and rookie Asa Newell would have to step into a larger role. Newell scored 13 points and grabbed four rebounds in his last outing, but he is not a proven starter yet. Atlanta is also missing rookie Kingston Flemings, who was suspended for one game after elbowing Bryce McGowens. The team needs Johnson to be the consistent “top guy” they currently lack. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
